title: Determiners
subject: english_grammar
syllabus_note: Follows the CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184) syllabus, Section B Grammar: determiners, tested through gap filling, editing and transformation.

blocks.title: A, the or nothing?
blocks.body:
Compare:

- *I saw **a** tiger.* (some tiger, any one)
- *I saw **the** tiger.* (the one we were talking about)
- *I saw **few** tigers.* (hardly any, a disappointing trip)
- *I saw **a few** tigers.* (some, a happy trip!)

The small words before a noun tell us *which* one and *how much*. They are called **determiners**. A tiny change (*few* → *a few*) can turn a sad sentence into a happy one.

Determiners are part of the CBSE grammar syllabus and appear in almost every gap-filling and editing question. Let's master them.

blocks.title: The storyteller of Malgudi
blocks.body:
R. K. Narayan created the imaginary town of Malgudi and filled it with unforgettable people: Swami and his friends, the guide Raju, the sweet-vendor Jagan. His English was simple and exact. Every *a*, *the* and *some* in his sentences was in the right place, so his stories read as smoothly as talk.

He won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1958 for *The Guide* and the Padma Vibhushan in 2000. His *Malgudi Days* was made into a much-loved television series.
blocks.future: Precise English opens careers in writing, publishing, film scripts, editing and translation.

blocks.question: Which sentence shows that the speaker is *pleased* with the number of friends who came?
options: A few friends came to my party.
Few friends came to my party.
No friends came to my party.
blocks.explanation: *A few* = some (a positive idea). *Few* = hardly any (a disappointing idea).

blocks.title: Words that come before a noun
blocks.body:
A **determiner** comes before a noun (and before any adjective) and tells us **which**, **whose** or **how many/how much**: *the* old *house*, *my* new *phone*, *three* red *apples*.

Two things decide which determiner to use:
1. **Countable or uncountable?** Countable nouns have a plural (*book → books*); uncountable nouns don't (*water, advice, information, furniture, luggage, news, money, knowledge*).
2. **Specific or general?** Do the speaker and listener know which one?

**Watch out:** *advice, information, furniture, luggage, equipment, homework, news* are uncountable in English: *some advice* (✗ *an advice*), *a piece of information* (✗ *informations*).

blocks.title: Kinds of determiners
blocks.body:
| Kind | Determiners | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Articles | a, an, the | ***an** honest man, **the** Ganga* |
| Demonstratives | this, that, these, those | ***these** books* |
| Possessives | my, your, his, her, its, our, their | ***their** house* |
| Quantifiers | some, any, much, many, little, a little, few, a few, a lot of, enough, several, no, all, most | ***a few** friends* |
| Distributives | each, every, either, neither, both | ***each** student* |
| Numbers | one, two, first, second, last | ***the first** prize* |
| Question words | which, what, whose | ***Whose** bag is this?* |

blocks.question: Which of these nouns is uncountable?
blocks.explanation: *furniture* has no plural: *some furniture, a piece of furniture*.
option_feedback: *chair* has a plural (*chairs*), so it is countable.

blocks.title: a / an: the sound decides
blocks.body:
**a** and **an** are used with **singular countable** nouns when we mean *any one* or mention something for the first time.

The choice depends on the **sound**, not the letter:
- **an** before a vowel **sound**: *an apple, an hour (h is silent), an honest man, an MLA (em-el-ay), an FIR, an X-ray*
- **a** before a consonant **sound**: *a book, a university (yoo-), a European (yoo-), a one-rupee coin (wun-), a uniform, a useful tip*

Other uses of *a/an*: jobs (*She is **a** doctor*), *per* (*fifty km **an** hour*, *twice **a** week*), exclamations (*What **a** beautiful day!*), and with *such* (*such **a** good boy*).

blocks.title: When to use the — and when to leave it out
blocks.body:
| Use **the** | Use **no article** |
|---|---|
| something already mentioned or known: *the book I lent you* | general plural or uncountable nouns: *Books are friends.* *Milk is good for health.* |
| unique things: *the sun, the moon, the sky, the earth* | names of people, cities, countries (most): *Ravi, Delhi, India* |
| superlatives and ordinals: *the best, the tallest, the first, the last* | meals: *We have lunch at one.* |
| rivers, seas, oceans, mountain ranges, deserts, groups of islands: *the Ganga, the Arabian Sea, the Himalayas, the Thar* | single mountains and lakes: *Mount Everest, Lake Dal* |
| newspapers, holy books, famous buildings: *the Times of India, the Gita, the Taj Mahal* | languages and subjects: *She speaks Gujarati.* *I love history.* |
| musical instruments: *She plays the sitar.* | games and sports: *He plays cricket.* |
| countries with Republic/Kingdom/States, or plural names: *the USA, the UK, the Netherlands* | *go to school/church/bed/hospital* for their main purpose |
| *the* + adjective = group: *the poor, the rich, the blind* | days, months, festivals: *on Monday, in May, at Diwali* |

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: He is ____ honest and hard-working officer.
option_feedback: *honest* begins with a vowel sound (the *h* is silent), so *an*.
We are not talking about a particular officer already known.
A singular countable noun (*officer*) needs an article.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: ____ Himalayas protect India from cold winds.
option_feedback: Mountain ranges take *the*; only single peaks (*Mount Everest*) take none.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: She studied at ____ university in Ahmedabad.
option_feedback: *university* begins with a *yoo* sound (a consonant sound): *a*.
Nothing tells us which university, so it is general.
A singular countable noun needs an article.

blocks.title: few, a few, little, a little, much, many
blocks.body:
| Countable (plural) | Uncountable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| **few** | **little** | almost none (negative feeling) |
| **a few** | **a little** | some, a small number/amount (positive feeling) |
| **the few** | **the little** | the small number/amount that there is, all of it |
| **many** | **much** | a large number / amount (mostly in questions and negatives) |
| **a lot of / lots of / plenty of** | **a lot of / lots of / plenty of** | a large number / amount (both) |
| **number of** | **amount of** | *a large number of people*, *a large amount of money* |

blocks.title: some / any / no, much / many, enough
blocks.body:
**some**: positive sentences, and offers/requests: *I have **some** money.* *Would you like **some** tea?* *Can I have **some** water?*
**any**: negatives and most questions: *I don't have **any** money.* *Do you have **any** questions?* Also *any* = it doesn't matter which: *Take **any** book.*
**no** = not any: *There is **no** milk.* (✗ *There is not no milk*)

**much** (uncountable) and **many** (countable): *How **much** sugar? How **many** eggs?* In positive sentences we usually say *a lot of*: *She has **a lot of** friends.*

**enough** goes before a noun: *We have **enough** chairs.* (but after an adjective: *old enough*)

**several** (countable, more than two): *several times*. **all, most, some, none of the** + noun: *Most of the students passed.*

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: There is ____ hope of finding survivors now; the rescue team is losing heart.
option_feedback: *a little* hope is positive; the team is losing heart, so the meaning is negative.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: Could you give me ____ information about the timings?
option_feedback: *information* is uncountable: *many* is for countable nouns.

sections.title: Each, every, either, neither, this, that

blocks.title: Distributives, demonstratives and possessives
blocks.body:
**each**: every one taken separately (two or more): *Each child got a gift.*
**every**: all of a group (three or more), seen together: *Every student must wear a badge.* *every day, every week.* (Never *every of*; say *each of* or *every one of*.)
**either**: one or the other of two: *You can sit on either side.*
**neither**: not one and not the other of two: *Neither answer is correct.*
**both**: the two together: *Both answers are correct.*
All of *each, every, either, neither* take a **singular noun and verb**.

**this / these** (near), **that / those** (far): *this book, these books, that house, those houses*. They must agree with the noun: ✗ *this books*.

**Possessives** (*my, your, his, her, its, our, their*) replace an article: ✗ *the my book*. And *its* (belonging to it) ≠ *it's* (it is): *The dog wagged **its** tail.*

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: There are shops on ____ side of the road.
blocks.explanation: *either side* = both sides of two (singular noun).
option_feedback: A road has two sides; *every* is for three or more.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The company has changed ____ logo.
option_feedback: *The company* here is treated as one unit (singular).

blocks.title: Gap filling with determiners
blocks.problem:
Fill in the blanks with suitable determiners:

*(a) ____ Ganga is (b) ____ longest river in India. It rises in (c) ____ Himalayas. (d) ____ year, millions of pilgrims take (e) ____ dip in its water, but (f) ____ of them think about keeping it clean.*
steps: (e) One single dip, first mention → **a** dip.
blocks.answer: The, the, the, Every, a, few

blocks.title: Editing determiner errors
blocks.problem:
Each line has one error. Correct it.

1. He gave me an useful advice.
2. I have less friends than my brother.
3. Mount Everest is a highest peak in the world.
4. Each students received a certificate.
steps: 1. *useful* starts with a *yoo* sound, and *advice* is uncountable: **an useful advice → some useful advice / a useful piece of advice**.
blocks.answer: some useful advice; fewer; the highest; student

blocks.question: Find the error: *I need an information about the trains.*

blocks.title: Remember determiners the easy way
blocks.body:
- **A/an: listen, don't look.** *an hour, a university, an MBA, a one-way street.*
- **"A" makes it positive:** *a few, a little* = some. Without *a*: *few, little* = almost none.
- **Few/many/fewer = count** (people, books). **Little/much/less = amount** (water, time).
- **THE for the ONE:** one sun, one best, one first, one Ganga, one Himalayas.
- **Each, every, either, neither → singular noun.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. ✗ *a hour* ✓ *an hour*; ✗ *an university* ✓ *a university*
2. ✗ *an advice / informations / furnitures* ✓ *some advice, information, furniture*
3. ✗ *less people* ✓ *fewer people*
4. ✗ *He is best student.* ✓ *He is the best student.*
5. ✗ *She plays the cricket.* ✓ *She plays cricket.* (but *plays the violin*)
6. ✗ *Every students* ✓ *Every student*
7. ✗ *the Mount Everest* ✓ *Mount Everest*; ✗ *Himalayas* ✓ *the Himalayas*
8. ✗ *this books* ✓ *these books*
9. ✗ *I don't have some money.* ✓ *I don't have any money.*
10. ✗ *it's own way* ✓ *its own way*

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Read out a short news report with every determiner removed and ask students to restore them. Then play **"few or a few?"**: the teacher says a situation (*Only two people came to the free concert*), and students hold up a card *FEW* or *A FEW* to show the feeling. Finish with an *a/an* sound race: *hour, union, MLA, one-day match, honour, European*.

blocks.title: Say it in your own words
blocks.body: Explain the difference between *He has little knowledge of computers* and *He has a little knowledge of computers*. Which one would help him get a job?

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Chapter 3, Concord:** *each/every/either/neither* take singular verbs; *a number of / the number of*.
- **Editing and gap filling:** article errors are among the commonest in the board paper.
- **Analytical paragraph writing:** *a large number of, a small amount of, the majority of, few, several* describe data precisely.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
Fill in the blanks:

*There was (a) ____ old man in our village who owned (b) ____ elephant. (c) ____ children loved (d) ____ elephant, but (e) ____ adults were afraid of it. Every morning (f) ____ man took it to (g) ____ river for (h) ____ bath.*

**Answer:** (a) **an** (b) **an** (c) **The** / *All the* (d) **the** (now known) (e) **some/many** (or *a few*) (f) **the** (g) **the** (h) **a**.

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- Determiners come before nouns and tell which, whose, how many or how much.
- *a/an* by sound; *the* for specific or unique things, superlatives, rivers, ranges, oceans, instruments.
- No article with general plurals, uncountables, names, meals, languages, games.
- *few/a few/many/fewer* with countables; *little/a little/much/less* with uncountables.
- *some* in positives, offers and requests; *any* in negatives and questions.
- *each, every, either, neither* + singular noun.

blocks.title: Board exam tips
blocks.body:
- Decide countable/uncountable first, then positive/negative meaning.
- Say the next word aloud in your head before choosing *a* or *an*.
- In editing, look for a missing *the* before superlatives, and for *a/an* before uncountable nouns.
- Remember the uncountables: *advice, information, furniture, luggage, equipment, news, knowledge*.

blocks.front: a or an: ___ hour, ___ university, ___ MLA?
blocks.back: *an hour*, *a university*, *an MLA*: the sound decides.
*few* = almost none (negative); *a few* = some (positive). Both with countable nouns.
Rivers: *the Ganga*. Single mountains: no article: *Mount Abu*.
